turns.doctor_question: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you into the clinic today?
turns.patient_response: I’m here because I can’t stop noticing this rough, sunken-looking patch on my face. In pictures and in the mirror, one side looks old and beat-up to me. Other people say they barely see anything, but I see it all the time.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient reports persistent preoccupation with a perceived rough, sunken facial patch that others barely notice.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself spending a lot of time each day doing things like checking it in the mirror, trying to fix or hide it, or asking others about it?
turns.patient_response: Yeah. Before work, or if I’m supposed to go to my sister’s game night, I can stand at the bathroom mirror checking it over and over—turning my face under different lights, rubbing at the spot. Sometimes I pull a hat down low, and sometimes I just make an excuse not to go if it looks too obvious to me.

symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient describes repeated mirror checking under different lights, rubbing at the perceived spot, concealing it with a hat, and avoiding events because of appearance concerns.

turns.doctor_question: Do you ever consider the possibility that you might be exaggerating this flaw, or are you completely convinced it is as bad as you see it?
turns.patient_response: I don’t know. I mean, people tell me it’s not that noticeable, so maybe they’re right, but when I look at it, it really does look bad to me. It’s hard for me to see it any other way.
